title: Japanese Pagoda Tree: Ancient Sophoras You Can Visit
meta_description: It flowers cream in August, when almost nothing else does, and despite the name it is Chinese. Twelve mapped, across eleven cities.
intro: This tree flowers cream in August, when almost nothing else in a European city is doing anything at all, and that habit is most of the reason it was ever planted. Despite the name it is Chinese rather than Japanese, brought into European gardens in the eighteenth century and set out in squares and courtyards where lunch happens outdoors. Vienna, Munich and the City of London each protect one. The oldest here is not European: the pagoda tree in the courtyard of Jogyesa in Seoul is put at 400 to 450 years, older than the temple hall beside it, and every Buddha's Birthday its crown disappears under thousands of paper lanterns. Kew's, planted in 1762, is one of the five veterans the garden's first curator nicknamed the Old Lions. Eleven cities so far, twelve trees.
